- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast gently to avoid undershoot.  
- If forecast peaks sharply after a spike in sentiment, apply a 1–2 day lag correction to smooth out over-optimistic peaks.  
- In multi-day trend continuation (e.g., 3+ consecutive days of rising prices), reduce forecast slope slightly to account for mean reversion.  
- If true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in early days of the 30d window, adjust future forecasts toward historical mean of last 7–10 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.3), avoid extrapolating trend; use 3–5 day moving average for smoothing.
